in_text_mentions: Brain MRI performed at the onset of the symptoms exhibited WM lesions in all patients, with patchy asymmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions involving subcortical and periventricular areas in five patients (Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 4 and Figure 5) and diffuse WM lesions in one subject (Figure 4) (Table 2).
There was a marked imaging improvement in all individuals (Figure 1 and Figure 2). Mild brain atrophy was present in two patients (Table 2).

Brain MRI features of five of the six patients shared similarities with ADEM, especially a patchy asymmetric distribution, which is uncommon in AGS [17] (Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3 and Figure 5). Diffuse homogeneous white matter lesions with brainstem involvement were seen in one patient with contrast enhancement, a feature, to our knowledge, never reported in AGS (Figure 4D,E). This patient with MRI signs of blood–brain barrier breakdown (patient 1) was the only one with a relapse four years after the first presentation, and he has the most pathogenic mutation. At 2.5 months of age biochemical and hematological parameters normalized, but hypotonia was still present. Ruxolitinib dose was increased to 0.4 mg/kg/day.
